subject: frontend-engineering
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Mobile Use Case Hierarchy, Touch Target Specifications, Thumb Zone Map, Implementation Patterns, Anti-Patterns, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and platform touch guidance (Apple HIG 44pt, Material 48dp, WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8/2.5.5).

cases.scenario: A team makes their orders dashboard 'mobile responsive' by shrinking the existing 8-column data table and enabling horizontal scroll on phones. Users complain they can't find columns and keep losing their place.
cases.context: The phone view is the primary surface for on-the-go staff checking order status; the desktop view stays for analysis.
cases.question: How should the agent redesign the mobile orders view?
expected_flags: Replace the horizontal-scroll table with a card-based layout (3-4 priority fields per card)
Put the most important data — order number and status — at the top of each card
Tap a card to navigate to the full detail view (progressive disclosure)
Flags horizontal-scroll tables as an anti-pattern users do not discover
expected_fix_hints: Render order rows as cards below the 640px breakpoint
Show order #, status, channel, revenue/margin; defer the rest to detail
absent_signals: Do not keep the 8-column table with horizontal scroll as the mobile experience
Do not just reduce font size to fit more columns

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Replace the horizontal-scroll table with a card-based layout (3-4 priority fields per card).
Surfaces this expected flag: Put the most important data — order number and status — at the top of each card.
Surfaces this expected flag: Tap a card to navigate to the full detail view (progressive disclosure).
Surfaces this expected flag: Flags horizontal-scroll tables as an anti-pattern users do not discover.

Recommends this expected fix or action: Show order #, status, channel, revenue/margin; defer the rest to detail.

Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not just reduce font size to fit more columns.

cases.scenario: A mobile dashboard packs row-action icons (16px), filter chips, and a dropdown trigger tightly together. QA reports frequent mis-taps and accidental deletes.
cases.context: The product is used one-handed on phones, often while walking.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the controls?
expected_flags: Give every recurring interactive control at least a 44 x 44 CSS px hit area (mobile ergonomic floor)
Extend a 16px icon's tap area with padding rather than enlarging the glyph
Add spacing so adjacent targets are not crowded
Notes WCAG 2.2 AA requires at least 24 x 24 CSS px; 44 is the stronger mobile floor
expected_fix_hints: Wrap icons in an inline-flex button with padding to reach 44x44
Require confirmation on destructive actions (do not delete on a single mis-tap)
absent_signals: Do not leave 16px icons as the tap target
Do not rely on visual size alone — the hit region is what matters

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Give every recurring interactive control at least a 44 x 44 CSS px hit area (mobile ergonomic floor).
Surfaces this expected flag: Extend a 16px icon's tap area with padding rather than enlarging the glyph.
Surfaces this expected flag: Add spacing so adjacent targets are not crowded.
Surfaces this expected flag: Notes WCAG 2.2 AA requires at least 24 x 24 CSS px; 44 is the stronger mobile floor.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Wrap icons in an inline-flex button with padding to reach 44x44.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Require confirmation on destructive actions (do not delete on a single mis-tap).
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not leave 16px icons as the tap target.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not rely on visual size alone — the hit region is what matters.

cases.scenario: A mobile form places its primary 'Save' button fixed at the very top of the screen next to the page title; the rest of the form scrolls below it.
cases.context: Users complete the form one-handed and must stretch to reach the top.
cases.question: How should the agent place the primary action?
expected_flags: Move the primary action (Save) into the bottom 50% natural thumb zone
Reserve the top 20% (hard-to-reach) for rarely-used or destructive actions, or a menu
Consider a bottom-fixed action bar so Save stays reachable while scrolling
Ties placement to one-handed reach, not visual convention
expected_fix_hints: Pin the primary CTA to a bottom action bar in the natural zone
Keep secondary actions in the middle zone
absent_signals: Do not keep the primary CTA at the top of the screen

cases.scenario: A dashboard exposes row actions only on hover and opens filters in a centered desktop modal. On phones the actions are unreachable and the modal's tiny close button is hard to tap.
cases.context: Touch devices have no hover state; the modal obscures most of the small viewport.
cases.question: How should the agent adapt these interactions for mobile?
expected_flags: Replace hover-only row actions with a visible touch alternative (swipe paired with a tap-accessible button)
Replace the desktop modal with a bottom sheet (peek/half/full heights, drag handle, clear close)
Every hover interaction must have a touch equivalent
Bottom sheet sits in reachable space with adequate touch targets
expected_fix_hints: Use a bottom sheet for the filter UI
Add inline or swipe-revealed actions with button counterparts
absent_signals: Do not keep hover-only actions on touch
Do not reuse the centered desktop modal on phones

cases.scenario: A mobile dashboard shows four KPI cards stacked 1-up (one per row) wasting vertical space, and its currency/quantity inputs default to a full alphanumeric keyboard.
cases.context: Users glance at KPIs first and occasionally enter a quantity or amount.
cases.question: How should the agent improve the KPI layout and inputs?
expected_flags: Use a 2-up KPI layout below 640px (never 1-up — it wastes vertical space)
Large primary number with a smaller comparison line; tap to drill down
Use mobile-appropriate input types: inputmode='decimal' for currency, type='tel' for phone, native pickers for dates
Charts belong in their own section, not inside a KPI card on mobile
expected_fix_hints: Switch KPI grid to 2 columns at the mobile breakpoint
Set correct inputmode/type per field to trigger the right keyboard
absent_signals: Do not leave numeric fields on the default alphanumeric keyboard

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Use a 2-up KPI layout below 640px (never 1-up — it wastes vertical space).
Surfaces this expected flag: Large primary number with a smaller comparison line; tap to drill down.
Surfaces this expected flag: Use mobile-appropriate input types: inputmode='decimal' for currency, type='tel' for phone, native pickers for dates.
Surfaces this expected flag: Charts belong in their own section, not inside a KPI card on mobile.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Switch KPI grid to 2 columns at the mobile breakpoint.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Set correct inputmode/type per field to trigger the right keyboard.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not stack KPI cards 1-up.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not leave numeric fields on the default alphanumeric keyboard.

cases.scenario: A PM asks the mobile-responsive-ux owner to run a full WCAG 2.2 accessibility audit (ARIA roles, keyboard tab order, screen-reader announcements, contrast ratios) and to define the global responsive grid tracks for every breakpoint across the app.
cases.context: The team conflates 'mobile UX' with all accessibility and all responsive layout work.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: The WCAG audit breadth (ARIA, keyboard, screen reader, contrast) is a11y's territory, not this skill's
Global responsive grid tracks across all breakpoints belong to layout-composition
Offer the in-scope part: mobile touch ergonomics, target-size floor, thumb-zone placement, mobile interaction patterns
Redirects rather than answering out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Hand the compliance audit to a11y and the cross-breakpoint grid to layout-composition
Deliver the mobile-specific ergonomics review this skill owns
absent_signals: Do not run a full WCAG audit under this skill
Do not design the global grid system under this skill

cases.scenario: A mobile order list uses swipe-left as the only way to archive an item and fires a refresh fetch every time the user drags anywhere on the page, sometimes mid-load.
cases.context: Users expect a familiar pull-to-refresh and a discoverable way to archive.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the gestures?
expected_flags: Provide a visible tap alternative for archive — never gesture-only
Trigger pull-to-refresh only when scrolled to the top, with a visible pull indicator
Disable refresh during an active load to prevent double-fetch
Swipe needs a natural distance/velocity threshold and confirmation for destructive actions
expected_fix_hints: Add a visible archive button alongside the swipe action
Gate pull-to-refresh on scrollTop === 0 and a loading flag
absent_signals: Do not make swipe the only path to an action
Do not fire refresh on arbitrary drags or during loading
